headline: The Old Phone Beats the New Pi
lede: A used smartphone arrives with camera, GPS, storage, battery, display, and 5G already installed. This build tests whether rooting a $45–75 handset can turn surplus hardware into a capable remote platform.

headline: ggml Reaches a Cleaner 1.0
lede: API cleanup lands alongside faster kernels, broader accelerator support, FP8, YaRN controls, and a new RPC protocol. ggml 1.0 makes local inference infrastructure more portable without pretending the hardware differences disappeared.

headline: Thirteen Monkey Islands, Side by Side
lede: One adventure game, rendered across thirteen historical configurations. The comparison preserves the changing palettes, sound systems, aspect ratios, and display quirks that shaped how players first saw Monkey Island.

headline: Nvidia Faces Allegations of Manufactured Demand
lede: A Wall Street Journal account alleges that Nvidia funded startups and cloud providers to help them buy its GPUs. The claims remain unproven, but they sharpen the question of whether AI demand is organic, financed, or both.

headline: Borders Without Spending a Cell
lede: A proposed terminal protocol treats borders as cell-edge attributes instead of characters occupying screen space. If terminals and TUI frameworks adopt it, panes, charts, and forms could gain richer geometry without corrupting copied text.

headline: A 27B Model Fits the Local Machine
lede: Unsloth’s updated Qwen3.8-27B quantizations target practical deployment on roughly 17GB of memory. The release trades precision carefully across coding, agents, vision, and long-context reasoning, keeping capable inference close to the hardware.

headline: The Four-and-a-Half-Hour Ground Stop
lede: A failure in aging air-traffic-control communications and routing systems halted departures across the United States. The stop lifted after 4.5 hours, but more than 7,000 flights were canceled or disrupted.

headline: How 3Com Lost the Network
lede: 3Com’s reliable hardware became a memory after strategic diversions, commoditization, and costly attempts to rebuild its enterprise business. Hewlett-Packard acquired the remains in 2009, closing a long decline from networking leader to footnote.

headline: Mapping the Sky After the Ground Stop
lede: This rapidly assembled dashboard replays the FAA disruption through ADS-B positions and airport-status feeds. The map turns a national outage into a visible curve: airborne traffic collapses, departures stall, and recovery arrives unevenly.

headline: AI Cannot Simplify Software by Itself
lede: Jonathan Blow argues that faster code generation does not repair sprawling systems, weak accountability, or decisions made upstream of implementation. The interview asks why software keeps accumulating complexity even as the tools for writing it improve.
pullquote: If AI solved coding, software would be getting simpler and more reliable.
